title: Trace invoke jobs (issue detection, GenAI evaluate, scorer): trace_ids must belong to the authorized experiment before any run or job is created
answers: Why can a user with write access to their own experiment run issue detection or evaluation on traces from another experiment?
Where is the check that stops a foreign trace id being scored or analyzed through the invoke endpoints?
Why does a rejected trace request leave no run or job behind in the MLflow server?
body:
Path: POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, /genai/evaluate/invoke and /scorer/invoke take caller-supplied trace_ids plus an experiment_id; the route validator only checks UPDATE on experiment_id. Chokepoint: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_trace_ids_in_experiment, called from _invoke_issue_detection_handler, _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler and _invoke_scorer_handler.
Rule: Any handler that queues a job on caller-given trace_ids must call _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment(store, trace_ids, experiment_id) before fetching credentials, resolving scorers or creating the run. It batch-fetches via batch_get_trace_infos and raises PERMISSION_DENIED (403, generic message) if any existing trace has a different experiment_id. Missing traces are not rejected here and fail later in the job.
Symptom: A user who owns experiment A could supply trace ids from experiment B; the job read those traces and wrote results into the caller's run in A.
Constraints: The guard lives in the handler, not the auth validator, so it also protects deployments that mount the handlers without the basic-auth app. Do not scope the batch lookup by experiment_ids, because that hides foreign traces and makes the check vacuous.
applies: Server-side job-invoking handlers in mlflow/server/handlers.py that accept trace_ids; not client-side SDK calls.
says: Users can run evaluation jobs on traces belonging to someone else's experiment
Prevent issue detection from analyzing traces outside the authorized experiment
Scoring traces from another workspace experiment should return a permission denied error
Trace analysis jobs should reject foreign trace identifiers before creating an experiment run
Running evaluations with invalid trace identifiers should not leave empty runs behind

The check batch-fetches traces via batch_get_trace_infos without scoping by experiment_ids and raises PERMISSION_DENIED (403) if any existing trace belongs to a different experiment_id, while missing traces fail later in the job. This guard protects POST endpoints /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke, /genai/evaluate/invoke, and /scorer/invoke in handlers rather than the auth validator, applying to server-side job-invoking handlers rather than client-side SDK calls.
